title: Best Stretch on a Ring
statement:
The numbers in `numbers` are arranged on a **ring**: after the last number comes the first one again. A **stretch** is a non-empty run of neighbouring numbers on the ring; it may go past the end and continue at the start, but it may not use any number twice.

Return the largest possible sum of a stretch.

examples.explanation: Start at the last 5, wrap around to the first 5: 5 + 5 = 10 (the -3 is skipped).
Every number is negative, and a stretch must contain at least one number, so the best is the single -2.

hints.nudge: A stretch that wraps around is a stretch that leaves out one stretch in the middle. What is special about the part that is left out?
hints.pattern: Kadane's algorithm twice: the best ordinary stretch, and (total - the WORST ordinary stretch) for the wrapping case.
hints.walkthrough: Checking every start and every length is O(n^2). There are only two kinds of stretches. One that does not wrap is an ordinary stretch: Kadane's algorithm finds the best one in O(n). One that wraps covers the numbers at both ends of the list and leaves out a middle stretch; its sum is total - (sum of the left-out middle stretch), so it is largest when the left-out stretch has the SMALLEST possible sum: run Kadane again with min instead of max. Take the larger of the two answers. One trap: if every number is negative, 'total - worst' would be 0, which would mean an empty stretch; that is not allowed, so in that case the answer is the ordinary best (the largest single number). O(n) time, O(1) memory.
